files.purpose: Self-monitoring for main-thread freezes: a dedicated background thread posts a block to the main queue every 0.5 s and, when the main thread has not answered for 4 s, runs /usr/bin/sample against the app's own pid and writes the captured stacks to ~/Library/Logs/Droppy Code/hang-<stamp>.txt. Its doc comment (lines 6-8) gives two reasons a force-quit freeze otherwise leaves nothing behind: "spindump declines for a development build, and the crash reporter never sees a process that was killed rather than crashed" (the second applies to release builds too). It stays on in every build because of its low cost (lines 15-16) and keeps at most 10 reports.

SOURCE FACT: the product name is hard-coded, not taken from AppInfo. reportsFolder() is `library.appendingPathComponent("Logs/Droppy Code", isDirectory: true)` (line 120) and the header literal starts `"Droppy Code main thread unresponsive for "` (line 91); the Logger subsystem is also the literal "iordv.droppycode" (line 18). A development build (AppInfo.isDevelopment, bundle id "iordv.droppycode.dev" in Text.swift) therefore writes into the same Logs/Droppy Code folder, and trimReports prunes one shared pool of 10 hang-*.txt files across release and development builds.
ui_elements: None. No visible UI; output is a log file and os_log entries only.
feature_notes: start(): under the lock, returns early if started is already true; otherwise sets started = true and lastPong = Date(), then starts the thread. Thread body: while true { Thread.sleep(forTimeInterval: 0.5); ping(); check() }.

ping(): DispatchQueue.main.async { lastPong = Date(); reportedThisStall = false }. While the main thread is stuck these blocks queue up; they all run once it recovers, which clears reportedThisStall so the next stall gets its own report (doc comment: "One report per stall; the next stall gets one of its own.").

check(): stalled = Date().timeIntervalSince(lastPong); returns nil unless stalled >= 4 (stallThreshold) and reportedThisStall is false; when it fires it sets reportedThisStall = true, so at most one report per stall. The seconds printed in the log (line 79) and the header (line 91) are this `stalled` value at the moment of detection, not the total length of the freeze: check() runs once per loop after `Thread.sleep(forTimeInterval: 0.5)` (line 52) and fires on the first tick with stalled >= 4, so with the watchdog thread on schedule the figure is about 4.0 to 4.5 (plus loop overhead) however long the freeze lasts. A port must print the detection-time value, not a measured total.
Log strings verbatim: "Main thread unresponsive for <stalledFor, .fixed(precision: 1)>s, sampling" and "Hang report written to <file.path, privacy .public>".

Sample failure paths: nonzero exit prefixes the body with "sample exited with status <N>" followed by two newlines; a throw from process.run() makes the body "sample could not run: <error.localizedDescription>" plus newline. The header is written in all cases.
Because writeReport runs on the watchdog thread synchronously, pings and checks pause for the ~2 s sample plus write time.

Doc comment rationale (lines 6-8): "the Dock asks spindump for a hang report, spindump declines for a development build, and the crash reporter never sees a process that was killed rather than crashed. So the app watches itself." Lines 15-16: "This costs a timer on a background thread and a block on the main queue every half second, nothing more, so it stays on in every build." No build-configuration gate exists in the file.

files.purpose: A shared namespace of three prebuilt Date.ISO8601FormatStyle values for parsing and writing ISO 8601 stamps that arrive from provider CLIs and GitLab, replacing per-call formatter allocation. It parses stamps with or without fractional seconds (trying fractional first, then plain), parses bare dates such as those from GitHub Copilot's quota endpoint, and writes whole-second UTC stamps with a Z suffix for filenames and prompts.

files.purpose: A main-actor JSON-RPC 2.0 client/server endpoint over a StdioProcess, used by Codex (which omits the jsonrpc member) and ACP agents (which require it). It correlates outgoing requests to responses by integer id through checked continuations, dispatches incoming requests and notifications to callbacks, answers unhandled requests with -32601, and fails all pending requests with the process's stderr tail when the stream closes.

feature_notes: request(): if isClosed throws RPCError(code: -32000, message: "The agent process is not running."). Otherwise id = .int(nextID), nextID += 1, checks cancellation, stores the continuation in pending and writes {"id", "method", "params"}. On task cancellation, a main-actor Task removes the pending entry and resumes it with CancellationError (no cancel message is sent to the agent).
write(): no-op when closed; drops "params" when it equals .null; adds "jsonrpc": "2.0" only when sendsVersion is true; sends .object(message).
notify() writes {"method", "params"}; respond(result) writes {"id", "result"}; respond(errorCode) writes {"id", "error": {"code", "message"}}.

handle(): non-object messages ignored. A message with a string "method" is a request if it has a parseable "id" (goes to onRequest; if onRequest is nil, responds with code -32601 and message "Method not found"), otherwise a notification to onNotification. Missing params become .null.

handle() responses: requires a parseable id with a pending entry, else ignored. If "error" exists and is not null, resumes throwing RPCError(code: error.code ?? -32603, message: error.message ?? "The agent returned an error.", data: error.data); else resumes with "result" ?? .null.

RPCID from a JSON double is `case .double(let id): self = .int(Int(id))` (line 10): Int(_:) truncates toward zero, so 3.0 and 3.7 both become .int(3), and Swift's Int(_: Double) traps (the process crashes) for NaN, infinity or a double outside Int's range (JSON text can carry an out-of-range number such as 1e300). This differs from JSONValue.int (JSONValue.swift line 86), which returns nil for a non-finite double. RPCID has separate `.int` and `.string` cases, so a string id "3" never matches a pending `.int(3)` and such a response is ignored.
start(): readTask iterates process.messages holding self weakly per message; when the stream ends calls didClose().

didClose(): once only; sets isClosed, tail = process.errorTail.trimmed, fails every pending continuation with RPCError(code: -32000, message: tail empty ? "The agent process exited." : tail), then onClose?(tail).

B1->B2: one line changed in didClose (line 144): process.errorTail.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines) became process.errorTail.trimmed (the new String.trimmed in Text.swift, which is the same whitespacesAndNewlines trim). No behavioural change.

close() is only `func close() { process.terminate() }` (lines 101-103): it does not set isClosed and does not fail `pending`. Pending requests fail only when process.messages ends and didClose() runs, which is at stdout EOF or 1 s after exit (StdioProcess.didExit asyncAfter 1 s -> finishOutput); if SIGTERM is ignored, exit itself waits for StdioProcess.terminate's SIGKILL at 3 s. In that window request() still passes the `if isClosed` guard, write() still sends, and StdioProcess.send enqueues `try? handle.write(contentsOf: payload)` on writeQueue after terminate()'s `writeQueue.async { try? handle.close() }`, so the write fails silently and the request waits until didClose().
unresolved_questions: JSONValue definition (equality with .null, .int/.double distinction, subscript on error objects) lives in another file and is not verified here.

files.purpose: The app's process-running and environment layer: Shell.run launches an executable off the main actor with a timeout, cancellation, optional stdin and optional per-stream tail limit, collecting stdout and stderr; ShellCommandKind classifies a shell command line as read-only or possibly file-writing so the timeline can skip working-tree snapshots for pure reads. It also defines OnceContinuation and the private OutputCollector, and LoginEnvironment, which captures the user's login-shell environment once (so Finder-launched apps find provider CLIs), augments PATH, resolves executables with which(), and picks the real developer git binary instead of the /usr/bin/git shim.

Shell.run: environment defaults to LoginEnvironment.current; stdin is a Pipe only when input is non-nil, otherwise FileHandle.nullDevice; readabilityHandlers are installed before run. A Mutex<Bool> 'cancelled' guards the race: under the lock, if already cancelled it throws CancellationError, else runs the process; onCancel sets the flag and terminates under the same lock. A deadline Task sleeps timeout seconds then terminates. After exit: cancels the deadline, checks cancellation, waits up to 3 s for both streams to hit EOF (collector.finished(within: 3)), checks cancellation again, returns ShellResult. A timed-out process returns its (signal) status rather than throwing.

Output limit: with outputLimit set, each stream keeps only its tail; append trims to the last 'limit' bytes once the buffer exceeds 2 x limit (amortized O(1) per byte, O(limit) memory). The run(tool:) overload does not pass outputLimit.
terminate(): returns if not running; SIGTERM via terminate(); after 1 s on a .utility global queue, if still running, kill(getpgid(pid) == pid ? -pid : pid, SIGKILL).

mayWriteFiles: empty after trim -> false; any ">", "$(" or backtick -> true; then splits on separators in order "&&", "||", ";", "|", newline, "&" (each replaced with U+0001), trims spaces per part, drops empties; true if any part is not onlyReads. onlyReads: tool = lastPathComponent of first token (empty part counts as read). sed reads only if some arg starts with "-" but not "--" and contains "n", and no arg starts with "-i" or "--in-place". awk/gawk/mawk read unless the part contains "system(". find/fd read unless an arg is in searchActions. sort reads unless an arg starts with "-o". git: first non-dash argument must be in gitReaders; bare git (no subcommand) reads. xcodebuild reads only with -showBuildSettings, -list, -version or -showsdks. swift, swiftc, node, npm, python, python3 read only when the arguments are exactly ["--version"], ["-version"] or ["-v"]. env reads only when every argument starts with "-". OnceContinuation: the continuation is taken out under the Mutex (set to nil in a defer) and resumed outside the lock, because (doc comment) a resume runs whatever the awaiting task does next and withLock is non-reentrant.

(2) OnceContinuation changed from @unchecked Sendable with an NSLock and a mutable optional to a checked Sendable class holding Mutex<CheckedContinuation<Value, Error>?>; take() now uses withLock with defer { continuation = nil }; a doc comment was added explaining take-under-lock, resume-outside. (3) OutputCollector changed from @unchecked Sendable with NSLock and four vars to Sendable with a private struct State (stdout, stderr, closed, waiters) inside Mutex(State()); reader, finished(within:) and close() rewritten to state.withLock with identical logic. The Synchronization import and LoginEnvironment were unchanged. No change to strings, timeouts, reader lists or classification rules.

run(tool:) (lines 121-133) resolves with `LoginEnvironment.which(name)` and no `in:` argument, so it searches LoginEnvironment.current["PATH"] even when the caller passes a different `environment` (that environment is used only for the child). It does not await LoginEnvironment.load(); before the login shell answers, current is fallbackEnvironment, so the search uses the fallback (augmented process) PATH. Only this overload produces ShellError("<name> was not found on your PATH.").

userShell() (lines 429-439): `ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["SHELL"]` is used only if `fileManager.isExecutableFile(atPath: shell)`, then `getpwuid(getuid())` pw_shell only if executable, otherwise "/bin/zsh".

Shell.run errors: a throw from `process.run()` (for example a missing executable) is rethrown as Foundation's own error through `once.resume(throwing: error)` (line 87), not a ShellError; a cancel before launch throws CancellationError (line 78). A timeout returns `process.terminationStatus` from the terminationHandler (line 74) with succeeded false. UNRESOLVED (Foundation runtime, not pinned source): for a child killed by a signal terminationStatus is expected to be the signal number (15 for SIGTERM, 9 for SIGKILL); Node on Windows reports exit code null plus a signal name, so a port needs an explicit mapping where callers compare status.
unresolved_questions: What the app does with a timed-out Shell.run result (it returns the terminated status, not an error) is decided by callers outside this file.
The sed rule treats any short flag containing "n" (e.g. -n, -En) as printing; a Windows port must decide whether to keep POSIX-only classification or add PowerShell rules; upstream has none.

files.purpose: Wraps a long-lived child process (a provider CLI or agent) that speaks JSON over stdio, either newline-delimited or with Content-Length headers, and exposes parsed messages as an AsyncStream. It serializes writes on a private queue, keeps a bounded stderr buffer whose last 4,000 bytes become the provider error text, tracks the exit status for waiters, and finishes the message stream when stdout closes or one second after the process exits.

feature_notes: send(): serializes message.data(); .lines appends a single 0x0A; .contentLength prefixes "Content-Length: <body byte count>\r\n\r\n". Encoding happens on writeQueue.
write(_:) sends raw bytes (doc: a prompt piped to a one-shot CLI); closeInput() closes stdin on the queue (for processes that read input to EOF before starting).

stdout handler: holds self weakly; if self is gone removes the handler; empty data (EOF) removes the handler and calls finishOutput(); otherwise consume(data) runs framer.append under the lock and delivers each message outside it.
deliver(): strips trailing 0x0D and 0x20 bytes, ignores empty lines and lines that fail JSONValue.parse, yields parsed messages.

stderr handler: on empty data or deallocated self, removes the handler; else appendError. errorBuffer is capped: when it exceeds 64,000 bytes it is cut to its last 16,000 bytes. errorTail is the UTF-8 decode of the last 4,000 bytes.
start(): installs both handlers and terminationHandler (weak self -> didExit(terminationStatus)) before run(); if run() throws, removes both handlers, finishes the message stream, and rethrows.
terminate(): always enqueues a stdin close; returns if not running; else process.terminate() and after 3 s on a global queue kill(pid, SIGKILL) if still running (pid only, not the group).
waitForExit(): returns the stored exit status immediately if known, else appends the continuation under the lock; the resume happens outside the lock.

didExit(): stores exitStatus, resumes all waiters with it, then (doc: a grandchild can inherit stdout and keep it open) after 1 s removes the stdout handler and calls finishOutput() again, so the message stream ends at most ~1 s after exit even if stdout stays open.
finishOutput(): delivers framer.finish() remainder if any, then continuation.finish(); it can run twice (EOF and the post-exit timer).

B1->B2: added import Synchronization; replaced NSLock plus four mutable properties (framer, errorBuffer, exitStatus, exitWaiters) with a private struct State held in Mutex<State>, initialized as Mutex(State(framer: StdioFramer(framing: framing))); errorTail, consume, finishOutput, appendError and didExit now use state.withLock; waitForExit replaced manual lock()/unlock() with withLock returning Int32? and resumes outside the lock. Numbers (4,000 / 64,000 / 16,000 bytes, 3 s kill, 1 s post-exit finish), framing and strings are unchanged.
unresolved_questions: Whether a second finishOutput() call can deliver a duplicate remainder depends on StdioFramer.finish() clearing its buffer (StdioFramer.swift, not in this bundle).
JSONValue.parse and JSONValue.data() encoding details (key order, escaping) live elsewhere.

files.purpose: A grab bag of app-wide text helpers: AppInfo exposes the display name, development flag, state directory name, version and build from the bundle; TextCleanup strips ANSI escapes, extracts last lines or a single line for error messages, and replaces em dashes and their relatives with hyphens in every model-written string. It also holds SimpleDiff, which builds a compact unified hunk with line counts for reported file edits (capped at 200,000 bytes), the FileEdit convenience initializer that uses it, and String helpers nilIfEmpty and the new trimmed.

feature_notes: stripANSI removes CSI sequences matching ESC [ params [0-9;?]* intermediates [ -/]* final [@-~].

lastLines: strips ANSI, `split(whereSeparator: \.isNewline)` (line 19), which splits on every Character with isNewline ("
", "", "
", U+000B, U+000C, U+0085, U+2028, U+2029), not only "
"; trims `.whitespaces` per line (spaces and tabs, not newlines); drops empty lines; returns the last count (default 4) joined by "
", or nil if none.

singleLine: `text.drop(while: \.isNewline)`, takes up to the next isNewline character, trims `.whitespaces` (spaces and tabs); if longer than limit (default 120) returns the first limit-1 characters plus U+2026.

withoutEmDashes: fast path returns the text unchanged unless the UTF-8 bytes contain E2 80 94 (U+2014), E2 80 95 (U+2015), E2 B8 BA (U+2E3A) or E2 B8 BB (U+2E3B) and a grapheme equals one of those; then maps each such Character to "-" keeping surrounding spaces. Doc examples verbatim (lines 37-40): "works — every time" reads "works - every time" and "ships—sometimes" reads "ships-sometimes" (U+2014 in both); "The en dash stays: it is the correct mark in a range, as in "lines 10–20"" (U+2013). Doc says it is applied to replies as they stream and land, thinking, plans, generated titles and commit messages.
mayContainEmDash byte scan: on 0xE2 reads the next byte; if 0x80 checks third byte 0x94/0x95, if 0xB8 checks 0xBA/0xBB; a truncated sequence returns false.

SimpleDiff.unified: `components(separatedBy: "
")` (empty text -> no lines; a text ending in "
" gets a trailing empty line that counts toward the numbers), trims common prefix and suffix lines, context of 3 lines before and after. Cap test `old.utf8.count + new.utf8.count <= diffLimit` (line 101): above 200,000 bytes returns Stats(diff: nil) with counts only; exactly 200,000 still emits a diff. Header "@@ -<oldStart>,<leading+removed+trailing> +<oldStart>,<leading+added+trailing> @@" where oldStart = prefix - leading.count + 1 (line 104). Reusing oldStart for the new side is correct, not a bug: leading = oldLines[max(0, prefix - 3)..<prefix] lies inside the common prefix, whose lines are identical and at the same indices in both texts, so the hunk starts at the same line number on both sides. ". Doc notes the same cap bounds command diffs (ThreadRuntime.fileEdits).
